title: Homemade Margherita Pizza with No-Cook Tomato Sauce
dek: A blistered, crisp-chewy crust carries bright crushed tomato, milky mozzarella, fresh basil and olive oil in a focused homemade pizza built for a very hot oven.
image_alt: Round Margherita pizza with a blistered golden crust, red tomato sauce, melted mozzarella and fresh green basil leaves
ingredients: 1 lb refrigerated pizza dough, preferably 60% to 65% hydration
1 tbsp fine semolina or cornmeal, for the parchment and pan
3/4 cup canned whole peeled tomatoes, drained for 5 minutes and crushed by hand
1/8 tsp crushed red pepper flakes, optional
8 oz fresh mozzarella, torn into 3/4-inch pieces and blotted very dry
1 packed cup fresh basil leaves, divided

instructions.name: Temper the dough and heat the oven
instructions.text: Set the dough in a lightly oiled covered bowl at room temperature for 45 to 60 minutes so it stretches without snapping back. Place an inverted heavy rimmed sheet pan on the upper-middle rack and heat the oven to 500°F for at least 45 minutes; the pan must be thoroughly hot before the pizza goes in.

instructions.name: Dry the mozzarella
instructions.text: Tear the mozzarella into 3/4-inch pieces, spread it on clean towels and blot firmly. Leave it uncovered while the dough warms. Removing surface whey keeps the center of the pizza from becoming watery.

instructions.name: Mix the no-cook tomato sauce
instructions.text: Stir the drained crushed tomatoes, garlic, oregano, 1/2 teaspoon salt, red pepper flakes if using and 1 tablespoon olive oil in a bowl. Keep the sauce uncooked and slightly textured; it will concentrate in the oven.

instructions.name: Shape without crushing the rim
instructions.text: Dust the dough and work surface lightly with flour. Press from the center outward, leaving a 3/4-inch border untouched, then lift and gently stretch the dough into a 12-inch round. If it resists, cover and rest it for 10 minutes before continuing.

instructions.name: Build the pizza sparingly
instructions.text: Set the dough on a 13-inch square of parchment dusted with semolina. Spread 1/2 cup sauce in a thin spiral, leaving the raised border bare. Scatter the dry mozzarella and Parmesan evenly, then tear over half the basil. Reserve the remaining sauce for another pizza or refrigerate it for up to 4 days.

instructions.name: Transfer to the hot pan
instructions.text: Slide the parchment and pizza onto the preheated inverted sheet pan, using a second cool sheet pan as a peel. Work carefully and keep hands clear of the 500°F metal. Close the oven immediately.

instructions.name: Bake until blistered
instructions.text: Bake for 8 to 11 minutes, rotating once after 6 minutes, until the crust is deeply golden with dark blisters, the underside is crisp and the cheese bubbles in browned spots. If the top needs more color, broil for 30 to 60 seconds while watching continuously.

instructions.name: Finish and rest
instructions.text: Transfer the pizza to a cutting board, drizzle with the remaining tablespoon olive oil and scatter over the reserved basil and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt. Rest for 3 minutes so the cheese settles, then cut into 8 wedges and serve hot.

why_it_works: A long preheat stores enough heat in the inverted sheet pan to set and brown the underside before the toppings can flood the crust with moisture.
Draining both tomatoes and fresh mozzarella controls water while preserving the fresh dairy-and-tomato character that defines Margherita pizza.
Leaving the outer rim untouched traps gas from the fermented dough, producing a crisp-chewy, blistered border without special stretching tricks.
swaps: A preheated pizza steel or stone can replace the inverted sheet pan. Follow its heat limit and slide the parchment directly onto the surface.
Use 6 oz low-moisture whole-milk mozzarella for a drier, stretchier cheese layer; shred it coarsely and distribute it evenly.
For a dairy-free pizza, use a meltable plant-based mozzarella and omit the Parmesan. Check the dough label if strict vegan preparation matters.
storage: Cool leftover slices within 2 hours and refrigerate in a shallow airtight container for up to 4 days. Reheat on a preheated sheet pan at 425°F for 6 to 8 minutes, until the center is steaming and reaches 165°F. Freeze individually wrapped baked slices for up to 1 month and reheat from frozen at 400°F for 10 to 14 minutes.
notes: Do not use all of the sauce simply to avoid leftovers. A restrained 1/2 cup prevents a soggy center and keeps the crust and cheese in balance.
Parchment rated to 450°F can darken at 500°F. Trim it close to the dough, keep it away from exposed heating elements and use a 500°F-rated sheet if available.
Fresh basil added before baking softens into the cheese; the second fresh addition supplies the vivid aroma and green finish visible on the finished pizza.

faqs.q: Why did my pizza dough keep shrinking while I stretched it?
faqs.a: The dough was still cold or its gluten was tense. Cover it and rest for 10 minutes, then continue gently. Bringing refrigerated dough to room temperature for 45 to 60 minutes prevents most snap-back.

faqs.q: How can I prevent a wet center with fresh mozzarella?
faqs.a: Drain and blot the cheese thoroughly, drain the tomatoes, and use only 1/2 cup sauce. Tear mozzarella into small pieces with space between them so moisture can evaporate in the hot oven.

faqs.q: Can I make this without a pizza stone or steel?
faqs.a: Yes. A heavy rimmed sheet pan heated upside down for at least 45 minutes creates a broad, hot surface and avoids the raised rim that makes transferring a pizza difficult.

title: Kimchi Fried Rice with Crispy Fried Egg & Scallions
dek: Cold rice, well-fermented kimchi and gochujang fry into a smoky-spicy skillet meal finished with sesame oil, scallions and crisp-edged eggs.
image_alt: Overhead bowl of red kimchi fried rice topped with a sunny crisp-edged fried egg, chopped green scallions and a dark savory sauce drizzle
ingredients: 4 cups cold cooked short- or medium-grain white rice, chilled at least 4 hours
1 1/2 cups well-fermented napa cabbage kimchi, drained and chopped into 1/2-inch pieces
1 tbsp vegetarian mushroom oyster sauce, divided
4 scallions, white and green parts separated and thinly sliced
1 cup frozen peas, thawed and patted dry
1 sheet roasted nori, cut into thin strips, optional

instructions.name: Break up the cold rice
instructions.text: Use damp fingers to separate the chilled rice into loose grains before heating the skillet. Cold, dry rice fries instead of collapsing into a sticky mass. Keep it refrigerated until the pan is ready.

instructions.name: Mix the seasoning
instructions.text: Whisk the kimchi brine, gochujang, soy sauce, 2 teaspoons mushroom oyster sauce and sugar in a small bowl until smooth. Taste the kimchi first; if it is especially salty, reduce the soy sauce to 2 teaspoons.

instructions.name: Sear the kimchi
instructions.text: Heat a wide 12-inch skillet over medium-high until hot. Add 1 tablespoon neutral oil, the onion and scallion whites, and cook for 2 minutes. Add the kimchi and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring only occasionally, until its edges darken and most visible moisture evaporates.

instructions.name: Fry the rice in a broad layer
instructions.text: Add the garlic and stir for 20 seconds. Add the cold rice and remaining seasoning mixture, spread everything across the skillet and leave it undisturbed for 90 seconds. Toss, spread again and cook for another 3 to 4 minutes until hot with scattered crisp grains.

instructions.name: Finish the vegetables and sesame
instructions.text: Fold in the peas and half the scallion greens and cook for 1 to 2 minutes, until the peas are hot and the rice reaches 165°F. Remove from the heat, drizzle with sesame oil and transfer to four warm bowls.

instructions.name: Fry crisp-edged eggs
instructions.text: Wipe the skillet clean enough to remove loose rice, return it to medium-high heat and add the remaining 2 tablespoons neutral oil. Crack in the eggs, season with salt and fry for 2 to 3 minutes until the whites are set and the edges are browned and lacy.

instructions.name: Check egg doneness for your diners
instructions.text: For a runny yolk, serve promptly once the white is fully set. For children, older adults, pregnant people or anyone with a weakened immune system, use pasteurized eggs or continue cooking until both white and yolk reach 160°F.

instructions.name: Garnish and serve
instructions.text: Stir the reserved teaspoon mushroom oyster sauce with 1 teaspoon warm water. Top each bowl of hot kimchi fried rice with one egg, drizzle lightly with the thinned sauce, and scatter over the remaining scallion greens, sesame seeds and nori strips if using. Serve immediately while the rice is hot and the egg edges are still crisp.

why_it_works: Well-fermented kimchi provides acidity, chile depth and savory complexity, while frying it until nearly dry concentrates flavor instead of making the rice soggy.
Chilled rice has a firmer, drier surface than freshly cooked rice, so its grains separate and pick up browned spots in a hot skillet.
Mixing the brine, gochujang and soy sauce before cooking distributes seasoning quickly, limiting the stirring that would otherwise soften the rice.
swaps: Brown rice or jasmine rice can replace short-grain rice as long as it is fully chilled and the grains are separated before frying.
For a vegan version, omit the eggs and add 8 oz diced extra-firm tofu after the kimchi; fry until browned before adding the rice. Confirm the kimchi is made without fish sauce or salted shrimp.
Frozen corn or finely diced carrots can replace the peas. Thaw frozen vegetables and pat them dry so they do not steam the rice.
storage: Rice should be cooled promptly after its first cooking and refrigerated within 2 hours in a shallow container. Refrigerate leftover kimchi fried rice without the eggs for up to 4 days. Reheat once in a hot skillet with 1 tablespoon water until every portion reaches 165°F; fry fresh eggs for serving. Do not leave cooked rice at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
notes: Kimchi flavor varies widely. Older, tangier kimchi is ideal here; fresh mild kimchi may need an extra teaspoon of brine and 1/2 teaspoon rice vinegar.
A 12-inch skillet gives four cups of rice enough contact with the metal to brown. If your pan is smaller, fry the rice in two batches.
This dish can be vegetarian only when the kimchi and gochujang labels confirm no fish sauce, anchovy extract or salted shrimp.

faqs.q: Can I use freshly cooked rice for kimchi fried rice?
faqs.a: Yes, but spread the hot rice on a rimmed sheet pan and refrigerate it uncovered for 30 to 45 minutes until cold and dry on the surface. Never leave it cooling at room temperature for an extended period.

faqs.q: Why is my fried rice soft and clumpy?
faqs.a: Warm rice, wet kimchi or an overcrowded pan usually causes clumping. Use thoroughly chilled rice, drain the kimchi, preheat a wide skillet and let each layer sit undisturbed long enough to fry.
With 1 tablespoon gochujang it is moderately spicy, though kimchi heat varies. Use 2 teaspoons gochujang for a gentler version or add another teaspoon at the table for more heat.

title: Pear Frangipane Tart with Almond Shortcrust
dek: Buttery almond pastry holds a tender frangipane filling and overlapping slices of pear in a polished autumn tart that can be made a day ahead.
image_alt: Golden round pear tart with overlapping pear slices in almond filling and a tall fluted pastry crust on a white plate
ingredients: 8 tbsp (113 g) cold unsalted butter, cut into 1/2-inch cubes

instructions.name: Make the almond shortcrust
instructions.text: Pulse 1 1/4 cups all-purpose flour, powdered sugar, 1/3 cup almond flour and 1/4 teaspoon salt in a food processor. Add the cold butter and pulse until the largest pieces resemble peas. Add the egg yolk and 2 tablespoons ice water; pulse just until the dough holds when squeezed, adding the final tablespoon water only if needed.

instructions.name: Chill the shaped shell
instructions.text: Press the dough evenly across the bottom and 1 inch up the sides of a 9-inch fluted tart pan with a removable bottom. Prick the base lightly with a fork, freeze for 30 minutes and heat the oven to 350°F with a rack in the lower-middle position.

instructions.name: Blind-bake the crust
instructions.text: Line the frozen shell with crumpled parchment and fill it to the rim with pie weights or dry beans. Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes, remove the parchment and weights, then bake for 6 to 8 minutes more until the base looks dry and the edges are pale gold. Cool for 15 minutes.

instructions.name: Beat the frangipane
instructions.text: Beat the softened butter, granulated sugar and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt for 2 minutes until creamy. Beat in 1 cup almond flour and 1 tablespoon all-purpose flour, then add the whole egg, vanilla and almond extract if using. Mix only until smooth.

instructions.name: Slice and season the pears
instructions.text: Peel and halve the pears, scoop out the cores with a teaspoon and cut each half crosswise into 1/8-inch slices while keeping the halves together. Brush the cut surfaces lightly with lemon juice.

instructions.name: Arrange the tart
instructions.text: Spread the frangipane evenly in the cooled shell. Fan each sliced pear half by pressing it gently at an angle, then slide a thin spatula underneath and transfer it onto the filling. Arrange the six fans in a circle and press them lightly into the frangipane.

instructions.name: Bake until deeply golden
instructions.text: Bake at 350°F for 38 to 42 minutes, rotating after 25 minutes, until the frangipane is puffed and golden, the pears are tender and the center reaches at least 165°F. A thin knife inserted between pear slices should emerge without wet batter.

instructions.name: Glaze without soaking the crust
instructions.text: Warm the apricot preserves with 1 teaspoon water until fluid, then strain if chunky. Brush a thin layer over the hot pears and frangipane, avoiding the outer crust so it stays crisp.

instructions.name: Cool before unmolding
instructions.text: Cool the tart in its pan on a rack for at least 45 minutes. Set the pan over a sturdy jar, let the outer ring fall away, then slide the tart from the base onto a serving plate. Cut with a sharp thin knife.

why_it_works: Freezing the shaped crust before blind-baking limits shrinkage, while weights support the fluted sides until their structure sets.
A partially baked shell forms a moisture barrier beneath the almond filling and pears, keeping the bottom crisp enough for neat slices.
Firm-ripe Bosc pears hold their fan shape in the oven, and a thin apricot glaze adds shine without obscuring the fruit.
swaps: Anjou pears can replace Bosc pears if they are firm-ripe. Avoid very soft Bartlett pears, which release more juice and lose their shape.
Orange marmalade warmed with a teaspoon of water can replace apricot preserves; strain it for a smooth, translucent glaze.
For a nut-free tart, use a standard pâte sucrée shell and vanilla pastry cream instead; almond flour cannot be replaced one-for-one in this frangipane.
storage: Cool completely before covering. Keep the tart at cool room temperature for up to 8 hours or refrigerate for up to 4 days. For the best crust, warm slices on a sheet pan at 325°F for 8 to 10 minutes; serve at room temperature or just warm. Freeze unglazed baked slices for up to 1 month, thaw overnight and refresh at 325°F before glazing.
notes: Weighing the flours is especially helpful here because almond flour settles differently from all-purpose flour and small ratio changes affect the crust.
The pears should yield slightly near the stem but remain firm enough to slice cleanly. Very hard pears stay chalky; overripe pears can flood the filling.
The 180-minute total includes freezing, blind-baking, cooling the shell and cooling the finished tart; active work is about 40 minutes.

faqs.q: Can I make the pear frangipane tart ahead?
faqs.a: Yes. Bake and glaze it one day ahead, cool completely and refrigerate loosely covered. Let it stand at room temperature for 45 minutes before serving, or warm slices briefly at 325°F.

faqs.q: Why did the sides of my tart crust slump?
faqs.a: The shell was probably too warm or the pie weights did not reach the rim. Freeze the shaped shell for a full 30 minutes and fill the parchment-lined crust completely with weights for the first bake.

faqs.q: How do I know the frangipane is fully baked?
faqs.a: It should be puffed, evenly golden and set between the pear fans rather than glossy or wet. The center should reach at least 165°F, and a thin knife should come out without raw batter.
